iterations.plan: Parse the ISO 8601 duration string by first validating the format, then extracting weeks/days and optional time components (hours, minutes, seconds), converting each to seconds and summing them.
iterations.feedback: Scores: {'correctness': 4, 'edge_cases': 2, 'spec_compliance': 2}. Weakest criterion: edge_cases. Problem: Zero durations such as 'PT0S' or 'P0D' wrongly raise ValueError because the check uses total_seconds == 0. Number parsing relies on float(), which accepts '1e3', 'inf', 'nan', '-1', ' 1', and '1_0'. Fractions are not restricted to the last component, so 'PT1.5H30M' is accepted. Fractions are also allowed on weeks and days when a time part follows, e.g. 'P1.5DT1H'. Weeks are accepted together with a time part, e.g. 'P1WT1H'. Component order is not enforced, e.g. 'PT1S1M' can slip through, and a string like 'PT1H' + '1M' is mishandled. Time-part garbage after H or M is not rejected cleanly.
